rationale: DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT. The `exports` verdict for Swift, pinned in both directions. MEASUREMENT behind the rule (400 tracked code-bearing .swift files of swift-corpus, pinned grammar, production path): 150 distinct node types produced, 0 of them naming an export declaration and 0 anonymous `export` tokens — so the export KEYWORD does not exist and any `exports` rule keyed on it would be dead code. The export CONSTRUCT does exist and is access control: 3777 `public` visibility_modifier tokens, of which 1381 sit on TOP-LEVEL declarations (543 nominal, 838 other) and 2326 on members; `open` is a separate token of the same class. `@_exported` (Swift's literal re-export attribute) occurs 2x in 400 files, too rare to be the rule. Therefore exports = top-level declaration whose access level is public or open, one edge per name. Family precedent for the relation itself: java derives JLS 7.6 'exported iff public' for top-level types, go derives capitalized package-scope names, python derives __all__. The FORBID half pins the three scope decisions (top-level only; never an extension; never a member; never the implicit `internal` default) so that widening any of them later breaks this fixture instead of passing it. SUPERSESSION (M14 swift lane, 2026-10-23) — THE SOURCE SPELLING ONLY; THE EXPORT SET IS UNCHANGED. This file pinned the exports SOURCE as the literal `root`. The standing ruling DERIV_EXPORTS_SWIFT4 makes the source the FILE'S LEAF NAME, and the SAME-CORPUS PASSING fixture swift/exports-visibility pins exactly that in BOTH directions: it EXPECTS `{"type":"exports","source":"exports-visibility","target":"Shape"}` and FORBIDS `{"type":"exports","source":"root","target":"Shape"}` with the measured reason '`root` is in parallel-indexer's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST so an edge sourced there can never bind to a stored symbol'. The two spellings cannot both be right, and the passing fixture plus the corpus-wide count (81 leaf-name vs 27 root) decide it. The six exports rows keep their targets and add the ruled vocabulary (`exportForm`/`accessLevel`/`evidenceClass`) and the NAME-node line numbers read off this file's own source with `grep -n`; a generic forbid on ANY root-sourced `exports` edge is ADDED, so the old spelling can never quietly return. Nothing was relaxed: the forbid half keeps every row, one row was added to the negative half, and no expected target moved. Predecessor kept byte-identical as module-exports.expectation.superseded-9b44d71469a24b14.json (`sha256 9b44d71469a24b14…`); the byte-identical corpus-import twin module-exports.expectation.superseded-e7c9819f4.json is left in place. The corrected rows are derived from the ruling and this fixture's source; the analyzer output was read only to CHARACTERIZE the defect.

forbidRelationships.comment: ADDED by the supersession: the source of a file-scope export is this file's leaf name, never the `root` literal. `root` is in parallel-indexer's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST, so an edge sourced there can never bind to a stored symbol — the same assertion swift/exports-visibility pins as `exports root -> Shape`.
